description:
## What

Pure rustdoc clarification. Document on the `now_unix` parameter that
it selects the moment at which validity-period checks are evaluated,
NOT the moment whose rules are in force. Catches the conceptual trap
exposed by the temporal-posture principle (PKIX-e3nl) before users
walk into it.

## Why

The 2026-05-13 chat surfaced an ambiguity in the existing API. Callers
may intuit that passing an older `now_unix` (e.g. `now_unix =
2024-08-15`) gives them "the rules in force at that older time."
It doesn't. It gives them the workspace's CURRENT BR snapshot,
evaluated at that older moment for validity-period checks only.

This is fine if documented; surprising if not. The temporal-posture
non-negotiable (PKIX-e3nl) explicitly calls this out — this bead
ships the corresponding API documentation.

## Sites to clarify

### `pkix-path/src/lib.rs`

- **`ValidationPolicy::new(now_unix)`** — add a paragraph stating:
  > `now_unix` selects the moment at which validity-period checks
  > (`notBefore <= now <= notAfter`) are evaluated. It does NOT select
  > which version of the rules are in force; the rules are always the
  > current set encoded in the surrounding `ValidationPolicy` fields.
  > For evaluation against rules in force at a past time, use
  > `pkix-policy-zlint` with a version-pinned lint set.

- **`Profile::policy(&self, now_unix: u64)` trait method** — add a
  paragraph stating the same semantic. The `now_unix` parameter
  is plumbed into `ValidationPolicy::new(now_unix)`; the contract is
  identical.

- **`pkix_path::validate_path(...)`** — link to the `now_unix`
  semantic on `ValidationPolicy::new` and/or restate it briefly. The
  function takes `&ValidationPolicy`, so the `now_unix` was already
  baked in when the policy was constructed; the clarification points
  callers back to the policy constructor.

### `pkix-profiles-cabf/src/lib.rs`

- Each `Profile` impl's `policy(&self, now_unix: u64)` — short note
  pointing to `ValidationPolicy::new`'s rustdoc. The Profile types
  don't add separate semantics for `now_unix`; they pass it through.
- Each free-function alias (`web_pki_policy`, `smime_policy`,
  `code_signing_policy`, etc.) — `# `now_unix` semantic` section
  pointing to the same clarification.

### `pkix-profiles` (RFC-baseline crate)

- Same clarification on `Profile::policy` impls and free-function
  aliases (`basic_tls_policy`, `basic_smime_policy`, etc.). Check
  whether the impls are thin pass-throughs that can link to the
  pkix-path doc, or whether they need their own copies.

### `pkix-chain` use-case wrappers

- `verify_tls_server`, `verify_smime_signer`, etc. — each takes
  `now_unix`. Document the same semantic on the wrapper's rustdoc.
  Pointing back to one canonical clarification is fine; the wrappers
  don't need to restate the whole thing.

## Acceptance

- All sites above have a `# now_unix semantic` paragraph (or
  equivalent inline note) clarifying validity-evaluation vs
  rules-in-force.
- One canonical, full statement on `ValidationPolicy::new`; all
  other sites can link back.
- Workspace-level `RUSTDOCFLAGS="--cfg docsrs -D warnings" cargo
  +nightly doc --no-deps --all-features --workspace` succeeds.
- No behavior change. CHANGELOG entries note pure-docs.
- Commit message: `docs: clarify now_unix is validity-eval moment,
  not rules-in-force moment (PKIX-e3nl)`.

## Out of scope

- Renaming `now_unix` or splitting it into two parameters (would be
  a breaking API change; the current name is correct under the
  clarified semantic).
- Adding a separate `rules_in_force_at` parameter to any API (out
  per PKIX-e3nl — the workspace doesn't offer that knob).

## Cross-references

- **PKIX-e3nl** (temporal-posture non-negotiable; this bead is the
  rustdoc half of the principle)
- **PKIX-4bip** (phased-rule helper catalog; sibling implementation
  bead; will reference this rustdoc once landed)
- existing `sc081_validity_cap` rustdoc, which already states the
  not_before_unix vs relying-party-clock distinction correctly —
  use as the model for the new clarifications

## Not blocked

This bead does not need to wait for PKIX-e3nl to land — the `now_unix`
semantic is true regardless of whether the principle is codified.
PKIX-e3nl makes the architectural reason explicit; this bead makes the
API surface match. Either can land first.
title: pkix-path / pkix-profiles-cabf: clarify now_unix rustdoc (validity-evaluation moment, NOT rules-in-force moment)
